security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel, S/U-mode code (or M-mode with MPRV) executes a cache-block management instruction (cbo.clean, cbo.flush, cbo.inval) targeting a virtual address whose PTE has R=0 or whose PMP region has R=0, or executes cbo.zero targeting a virtual address whose PTE has W=0 or whose PMP region has W=0. The hardware now explicitly raises a load/store page-fault or access-fault where previously non-enforcement was implementation-defined, exposing kernel assumptions that CBO operations succeed without explicit permission checks.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: (CBO_ZERO|CBO_INVAL|CBO_CLEAN|CBO_FLUSH)\s*\(.*\) without prior PTE permission validation (pte_write|pte_read) on the target address; or userspace-accessible code path issuing CBO without PTE R/W checks
security_spec.summary: CBO instructions are now unambiguously permission-checked: cbo.clean/flush/inval consume read permission, cbo.zero consumes write permission at both PTE and PMP levels, closing hardware-level privilege-escape vectors where implementations could silently allow cache-block operations across permission boundaries

findings.finding: Uses phys_to_virt() to convert DMA physical address to direct-map virtual address, then ALT_CMO_OP(CLEAN). The direct map always has R=1,W=1 PTE permissions for RAM pages, so cbo.clean (which requires PTE R=1 per supervisor.adoc norm:load_page_fault_no_r) is satisfied. Physical addresses come from the DMA API, not userspace — this is trusted kernel infrastructure.

spec_citations.excerpt: Attempting to execute a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction whose effective address lies within a page without read permissions raises a load page-fault exception.

findings.finding: Same pattern as arch_dma_cache_wback — phys_to_virt() into direct map, then ALT_CMO_OP(INVAL). The direct map provides R=1,W=1 for all RAM pages. cbo.inval requires PTE R=1, which the direct map satisfies. No software-side PTE validation performed, but none needed for kernel direct-map addresses.

spec_citations.excerpt: Attempting to execute a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction whose effective address lies within a page without read permissions raises a load page-fault exception.

findings.finding: Uses phys_to_virt() into direct map then ALT_CMO_OP(FLUSH). cbo.flush requires PTE R=1. The kernel direct map always provides R=1 for RAM pages, so this is safe. No software PTE walk performed, but the direct-map invariant makes it unnecessary.

spec_citations.excerpt: Attempting to execute a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction whose effective address lies within a page without read permissions raises a load page-fault exception.

findings.finding: Uses page_address() to get the kernel virtual address of a coherent DMA page, then ALT_CMO_OP(FLUSH). Pages from the DMA coherent allocator are kernel-owned and have full R+W in the direct map. cbo.flush requirement of PTE R=1 is satisfied.

spec_citations.excerpt: Attempting to execute a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction whose effective address lies within a page without read permissions raises a load page-fault exception.

findings.finding: Issues cbo.clean via ALT_CMO_OP(CLEAN) on PMEM virtual addresses from the NVDIMM subsystem. These are kernel virtual addresses with valid PTE mappings. cbo.clean requires PTE R=1, which kernel-mapped PMEM pages provide. The non-standard cache ops fallback uses virt_to_phys() to convert to physical addresses, bypassing MMU — this also relies on PMP being correctly configured.

spec_citations.excerpt: Attempting to execute a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction whose effective address lies within a page without read permissions raises a load page-fault exception.

findings.finding: Issues cbo.inval via ALT_CMO_OP(INVAL) on PMEM virtual addresses. cbo.inval requires PTE R=1 per spec. Kernel-mapped PMEM pages satisfy this. No software PTE validation, but addresses are kernel-internal.

spec_citations.excerpt: Attempting to execute a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction whose effective address lies within a page without read permissions raises a load page-fault exception.

findings.finding: Uses CBO_ZERO in an unrolled loop to zero pages from the buddy allocator. cbo.zero requires PTE W=1 per supervisor.adoc norm:store_page_fault_no_w. Pages from the buddy allocator are kernel-owned and always have W=1 in the direct map. The function performs no software W-bit validation because it trusts the caller (kernel page allocator). Block-size check at patches ensures the unrolled loop is only used when riscv_cboz_block_size <= 4K.
findings.snippet:
SYM_FUNC_START(clear_page)
	li	a2, PAGE_SIZE
	CBOZ_ALT(12, "j .Lno_zicboz", "nop")
	lw	a1, riscv_cboz_block_size
	add	a2, a0, a2
.Lzero_loop:
	CBO_ZERO(a0)

spec_citations.excerpt: Attempting to execute a store, store-conditional, AMO, or cache-block zero instruction whose effective address lies within a page without write permissions raises a store page-fault exception.

findings.finding: T-Head C9xx erratum: uses non-standard CMO instructions (THEAD_INVAL_A0) operating on physical addresses directly, bypassing MMU translation entirely. Registered as noncoherent_cache_ops.inv and called instead of ALT_CMO_OP when CONFIG_ERRATA_THEAD_CMO is set. Physical-address CMO relies on PMP for access control; the kernel configures its own PMP entries at boot. No PTE checks possible since MMU is bypassed.

spec_citations.excerpt: Attempting to execute a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction which accesses a physical address within a PMP region without read permissions raises a load access-fault exception. Attempting to execute a store, store-conditional, AMO, or cache-block zero instruction which accesses a physical address within a PMP region without write permissions raises a store access-fault exception.

findings.finding: Unconditionally sets ENVCFG_CBZE and ENVCFG_CBCFE for init task (current->thread.envcfg), which propagates to all userspace processes via fork() and context switch (__switch_to_envcfg in switch_to.h:84-88). This enables cbo.zero (requires PTE W=1), cbo.clean, and cbo.flush (require PTE R=1) for ALL userspace processes without any per-process opt-in. The spec (cmo.adoc norm:cbm_unperm_fault, norm:cbz_unperm_fault) mandates hardware raises page-faults when PTE permissions are insufficient, and the spec notes this enforcement was previously implementation-defined. On hardware with incomplete CBO permission enforcement, userspace could exploit cbo.zero on read-only mappings or cbo.clean/flush on inaccessible pages. cbo.inval (ENVCFG_CBIE) is correctly NOT enabled for userspace.

spec_citations.excerpt: A cache-block management instruction is permitted to access the specified cache block whenever a load instruction or store instruction is permitted to access the corresponding physical addresses. If access to the cache block is not permitted, a cache-block management instruction raises a store page-fault exception if address translation does not permit any access or raises a store access-fault exception otherwise.

A cache-block zero instruction is permitted to access the specified cache block whenever a store instruction is permitted to access the corresponding physical addresses. If access to the cache block is not permitted, a cache-block zero instruction raises a store page-fault exception if address translation does not permit write access or raises a store access-fault exception otherwise.

findings.finding: The ALT_CMO_OP macro emits CBO instructions via the RISC-V ALTERNATIVE framework, iterating over cache-block-aligned virtual addresses. It performs address alignment ((_start) & ~((_cachesize) - 1UL)) and loops by incrementing by _cachesize until reaching (_start + _size). No PTE permission validation is performed within the macro — the caller is responsible. This is correct architectural design: PTE enforcement is the hardware's responsibility; the macro is infrastructure, each call site is responsible for address validity.
findings.snippet:
#define ALT_CMO_OP(_op, _start, _size, _cachesize)
asm volatile(ALTERNATIVE(
	__nops(5),
	"mv a0, %1\n\t"
	"j 2f\n\t"
	"3:\n\t"
	CBO_##_op(a0)
	"add a0, a0, %0\n\t"
